title: Binomial Theorem
prerequisites: Algebraic identities such as (a + b)² and (a + b)³.
Ability to simplify expressions with powers.

topics.title: Binomial Expansion and General Term
topics.quick_summary: The binomial theorem expands (a + b)ⁿ as a sum of n + 1 terms whose coefficients are the combinations ⁿCᵣ.
topics.real_life: Compound interest, probability distributions and approximations in physics all rely on binomial expansions rather than repeated multiplication.

detailed.definition: For any positive integer n, (a + b)ⁿ = Σ ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ for r = 0 to n. The general term is Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ.
detailed.key_idea: The general term is indexed Tᵣ₊₁, not Tᵣ, because r starts at 0. This off-by-one is the single most common error in the whole chapter.
detailed.working_principle: The powers of a decrease from n to 0 while the powers of b increase from 0 to n, and in every term the two powers add to n — a useful check on any expansion.
applications: The expansion has exactly n + 1 terms.
The coefficients are the entries of the nth row of Pascal's triangle.
Coefficients equidistant from the two ends are equal, since ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ.

points: General term Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ.
Number of terms in the expansion = n + 1.
The sum of the exponents in each term is always n.
For (a − b)ⁿ the signs alternate, starting positive.
mistakes: Writing the general term as Tᵣ instead of Tᵣ₊₁.
Forgetting the alternating signs in (a − b)ⁿ.
Using n instead of n + 1 for the number of terms.
topics.memory_hook: 'Powers of a fall, powers of b rise, and together they always add to n.'
topics.advanced: Newton extended the theorem to negative and fractional exponents, where the expansion becomes an infinite series valid for |x| < 1. That generalisation is the basis of most approximation formulas in physics.

formulas.name: Binomial Theorem
formulas.variables: a and b = the two terms, n = positive integer exponent, r = term index.
formulas.when_to_use: To expand a binomial power or to find one particular term without expanding fully.
formulas.common_mistakes: Interchanging the powers of a and b.
formulas.shortcut: For the middle term of an even power n, take r = n/2.

formulas.name: General Term
formulas.variables: r = 0, 1, 2, ..., n; Tᵣ₊₁ is the (r+1)th term.
formulas.when_to_use: To find a specific term, the term independent of x, or the coefficient of a given power.
formulas.common_mistakes: Setting r equal to the required term number instead of one less.
formulas.shortcut: For the term independent of x, set the total power of x to zero and solve for r.
